llm.summary: This skill is for Douyin tourism reports, but its subscription and report-generation code creates avoidable security risks that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network access to RedFoxHub, local report writes, browser opening, and use of user-level schedulers fit the feature set but are high-impact enough to need tighter scoping and safer handling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no hidden install hook in the inspected artifacts; setup asks for requests and a RedFox API key. The documentation also shows a plaintext config-file option for the key.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Trigger guidance is broad and the skill instructs agents to automatically open generated HTML reports; side-effecting actions such as external API calls, file creation, browser launch, and subscriptions are not consistently gated by explicit confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The subscription feature writes a macOS LaunchAgent or crontab entry for recurring execution, and the macOS path may copy REDFOX_API_KEY into a plaintext plist.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of fetching Douyin cultural-tourism data and generating HTML reports is coherent, and daily subscription is disclosed, but verified code allows user/API content into shell commands and HTML without safe escaping.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and are comfortable with RedFoxHub API queries, local HTML report files, and optional recurring scheduled jobs. Avoid subscription mode until shell handling, HTML escaping, and credential storage are fixed; prefer one-time runs with a revocable API key and do not open reports from untrusted data automatically.
llm.findings:
[P2] expected: The cited HTML comment is a normal font/template comment, not an artifact-backed prompt-injection instruction.
[TM1] unexpected: The shell-based crontab removal command is real and unsafe; command construction with shell=True is not necessary for the stated purpose.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad natural-language trigger guidance can invoke external fetching and report creation from loosely related prompts without clear activation boundaries.
[SQP-2] expected: Recurring subscriptions, third-party API queries, local HTML output, and auto-open behavior are part of the product, but the disclosures and user controls are incomplete.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese locale and fixed Chinese output are consistent with the China/Douyin-focused use case and are not independently suspicious.
[LP3] expected: The required capabilities are mostly purpose-aligned, but there is no clear least-privilege boundary around shell, network, file output, browser launch, and credential access.
[RA2] expected: Persistence is disclosed as daily subscription, but it uses OS-level scheduled tasks and stores or reuses credentials across sessions, so it remains a material review concern.
[SDI-1] expected: Subscription scheduling is described in the skill and READMEs, so it is not hidden, but the concrete LaunchAgent/crontab implementation is high-impact.
[T06] expected: The LaunchAgent/crontab persistence finding is verified and purpose-related, but needs explicit informed consent, listing/removal controls, and safer scoping.
[T09] unexpected: The command-injection, stored HTML-injection, and plaintext credential-storage findings are supported by the inspected code and are not required for the feature to work.
